claims.text: The 5.00 SGD fee cannot stand because the driver never satisfied POL-NS-23's contact obligation, which is conjunctive: before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05070) contains no driver-authored message before the 16:13:40 cancellation, and the trip record's derived contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 with an empty messages array, while its own 'obligation_met' value is false. The message limb fails, so POL-NS-23 voids the fee: FULL_REFUND of the fee charged with no driver compensation.

The only pre-cancellation entry in the entire chat log is MSG-05070-001 at 16:07:28, 'Your driver has arrived.' That entry's sender is SYSTEM - the app's automatic arrival notification - and POL-NS-23 requires a chat message the driver sent to the rider. A machine-generated notification is not a driver message, and the driver's own statement concedes the point by relying on the fact that 'the app also sends the arrived notification automatically'.

The driver's assertion that he 'also sent message' is contradicted on the record. The chat log is COMPLETE with no issues at weight 1.0, contiguous and matching trip_record.chat_message_count = 3; the only driver-authored message, MSG-05070-002 ('I cancel already, you never come down'), was sent at 16:13:55 - fifteen seconds AFTER the 16:13:40 cancellation. POL-NS-23 requires the message to precede trip_record.cancelled_at, so a post-cancellation message cannot cure the omission.

The two in-app calls at 16:09:30 and 16:11:50 (both unanswered, recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls) satisfy only the call limb of POL-NS-23. The clause states the obligation in the conjunctive and does not excuse the message limb where the rider could not be reached by phone - on the rider's account she was in the shower. The driver sent no message on the in-app channel at all before cancelling, so the fee is voided.

Escalation under POL-GEN-26 is not available on this record: the fact POL-NS-23 turns on - whether the driver messaged before cancelling - is carried by two COMPLETE artifacts, the trip record and the chat log, each with no issues and weight 1.0, so nothing on that point is missing or impaired. The one absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05070-01, is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) and carries nothing about in-app contact. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band, and neither party carries a fraud flag, so this case is decidable on the record.

Party history is context only under POL-GEN-01: ratings, account ages, cancellation rates and prior flags on either profile can neither establish a fact about TRP-05070 nor decide it. The only profile fields the policy permits to do anything are the two fraud-flag fields (POL-GEN-22, which raises the confidence an AI ruling needs and never decides a trip) and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d (POL-NS-25, a referral that never changes the ruling) - and no fraud flag is set on either party. The outcome therefore turns on the contact record alone.

The ruling follows directly from the voided fee. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00 SGD and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the rider has not been made whole. Under POL-GEN-03 the rider, as the filing party, is entitled to the whole contested amount - FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD with driver_compensation_sgd null - and POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome is confined to the case 'where the fee stands', which it does not.

claims.text: The driver was physically at the pickup when he marked arrival, and the GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.16 m away — well inside the STANDARD zone's 50 m arrival radius — the driver reports 25 fixes with no gap over 120 s, and the trace shows his vehicle stationary at the pickup from 16:07:20 onward. POL-NS-21's arrival test is therefore satisfied: the trip record's arrival event (16:07:25) is GPS-corroborated.

The free wait was fully served. The driver arrived at 16:07:25, the 300 s free wait ran to 16:12:25, and he did not cancel until 16:13:40 — 375 s after arrival and 75 s after the wait expired. On the on-demand branch of POL-NS-21 (no scheduled time, so the wait runs from arrival), the driver cancelled only after the policy-mandated wait had elapsed.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on the record: the driver placed two in-app calls to the rider, at 16:09:30 (rang 25 s, unanswered) and 16:11:50 (rang 20 s, unanswered), both inside the free-wait window and both before the 16:13:40 cancellation. These are in-app calls recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls, exactly the form POL-NS-23 requires.

The substantive ground for a no-show charge is made out independently of the contact formality: the rider never boarded, and her own only chat reply — 'What? I was coming down now' — was sent at 16:14:30, after both the expiry of the free wait and the cancellation. Where the no-show fee stands, POL-NS-22 fixes the outcome as DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd each equal to the 5.00 SGD charged, and POL-GEN-03 confirms that is a driver-side win, not a restoration of a charge.

The amount charged is exactly the amount the policy schedules: the payments ledger shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, matching POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee, and the fee-matches-policy derivation is true. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check has nothing to act on, so no referral on the amount arises and the fee is not exposed to a discrepancy argument.

I do not press — and must honestly concede — the message limb of POL-NS-23. The complete chat log (3 entries, contiguous, weight 1.0, matching trip_record.chat_message_count) carries no driver in-app message before the 16:13:40 cancellation: the driver's only message, 'I cancel already, you never come down', is timestamped 16:13:55 (15 s after cancellation), and the 16:07:28 'Your driver has arrived.' entry is a SYSTEM notification, not a message sent by the driver. The driver's counterparty statement that he 'sent message' is therefore corroborated only as to the two calls, not as to any pre-cancellation message, and on the strict terms of POL-NS-23 that limb is absent from this record.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged on TRP-05070 does not stand, and the rider is refunded the whole contested amount. The clause that decides this is POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3). Before cancelling for a no-show the driver must have done two things before trip_record.cancelled_at: sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call. The obligation is conjunctive. The call limb is met — the trip record (EV-TRIP-05070) shows two in-app calls placed by the driver at 16:09:30 and 16:11:50, both unanswered, both before the 16:13:40 cancellation. The message limb is not met. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05070) is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and contains no message sent by the driver before the cancellation. Its only pre-cancellation entry, MSG-05070-001 at 16:07:28 ('Your driver has arrived.'), has sender SYSTEM: it is the app's automatic arrival notification, not a message the driver sent. The driver's one own message, MSG-05070-002 ('I cancel already, you never come down'), was sent at 16:13:55, fifteen seconds AFTER he cancelled at 16:13:40. The driver's counterparty statement that he 'sent message' is not borne out by the record, and his own reference to the automatic arrival notification confirms that entry is the app's. I accept the driver advocate's concession on this limb. Because one of the two required contacts is missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee. The ledger (EV-FARE-05070) shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider has not been made whole. The rider filed, and she is owed the full amount: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with driver_compensation_sgd null. On the driver's points: the arrival was genuine and I accept it — EV-GPS-05070 and EV-TRIP-05070 satisfy POL-NS-21's arrival test, the nearest fix being 2.16 m from the pickup inside the STANDARD 50 m radius, and the free wait ran 375 s from arrival to cancellation, past the 300 s wait. But those are separate conditions and do not cure the failed contact obligation. Where the fee does not stand, POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome — which applies only 'where the fee stands' — has nothing to operate on, and POL-GEN-03 confirms that figure would be a driver-side award, not available here. On referrals: the amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 schedules, so its fee-amount check adds nothing. POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire — it requires the driver to have failed to arrive by the scheduled deadline and to have failed to attempt contact, whereas this on-demand trip has no scheduled time and the driver both arrived and called. POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show flag does not fire — rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not present, and the fee does not stand to be counted. No referral arises. Party history (ratings, account ages, prior flags on either profile) is context only under POL-GEN-01 and decides nothing. Neither party carries a fraud flag; the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final. My confidence is 0.95: the deciding fact — that no driver message preceded the cancellation — rests on the chat log and the trip record, both complete at weight 1.0, and the reader should note POL-GEN-02's cap is the weight of the carriers of that fact, not the bundle mean.

ruling.explanation:
The rider's claim succeeds and the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee is refunded in full.

DECIDING POINT — the driver's contact obligation (POL-NS-23). The clause is conjunctive: before cancelling for a no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call, each before trip_record.cancelled_at; if either is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged. The call limb is met — the trip record shows two in-app calls, at 16:09:30 (rang 25 s unanswered) and 16:11:50 (rang 20 s unanswered). The message limb is not met. The chat log EV-CHAT-05070 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issues, contiguous and matching trip_record.chat_message_count = 3. Its only pre-cancellation entry is MSG-05070-001, sent 16:07:28 with sender SYSTEM ('Your driver has arrived.') — the app's automatic arrival notification, not a message the driver sent. The driver's only authored message, MSG-05070-002 ('I cancel already, you never come down'), was sent at 16:13:55, fifteen seconds AFTER the 16:13:40 cancellation, so it cannot cure the omission. The trip record's own derived contact-before-cancel block agrees: message_count 0, empty messages array, obligation_met false. The driver's counterparty statement that he 'sent message' is contradicted by the complete log, and in any event POL-NS-23 reads the chat log and the trip record, not a party's account; the statement itself concedes that the arrival notification was 'automatic'. Because one limb of the conjunctive obligation is missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee.

THE DRIVER'S POINTS, ACCEPTED BUT NOT DECISIVE. (1) Arrival: accepted. The GPS trace EV-GPS-05070 corroborates the 16:07:25 arrival event — the nearest fix is 2.16 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, with 25 fixes and no gap over 120 s. (2) Free wait: accepted. On this on-demand trip (no scheduled time) the 300 s wait ran from arrival at 16:07:25 to 16:12:25, and the driver did not cancel until 16:13:40 — 375 s after arrival, 75 s after the wait expired. (3) The substantive no-show ground and POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome: rejected. POL-NS-22 fixes DRIVER_COMPENSATION only 'where the fee stands', and the fee does not stand, because POL-NS-23 voids it. The rider's late reply at 16:14:30 does not change that. (4) Fee amount: accepted. The payments ledger EV-FARE-05070 shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, exactly matching POL-NS-22's scheduled 5.00 SGD, so the clause's fee-amount check has nothing to act on.

REFERRALS. None arise. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not fire — the driver did arrive and did attempt contact (two calls), so its condition is not met. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not fire — the rider's profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, and the fee does not stand so this trip is not counted. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire because the amount charged equals the policy fee.

ESCALATION NOT AVAILABLE. POL-GEN-26 does not apply: the fact POL-NS-23 turns on — whether the driver messaged before cancelling — is carried by two COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (the trip record and the chat log). The only absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05070-01 (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), says nothing about in-app contact and carries no fact.

CONFIDENCE AND WHO DECIDES. Party history is context only under POL-GEN-01 and neither profile carries a fraud flag. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final (POL-NS-26). Confidence 0.95, within the cap set by POL-GEN-02(2) — the deciding fact is carried by the chat log and the trip record, each at weight 1.0.

OUTCOME. The rider, who filed, is owed the whole contested amount: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with no driver compensation (driver_compensation_sgd null). The figures used are the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged (EV-FARE-05070) and the 5.00 SGD policy fee (POL-NS-22).

ledger.claim: The 5.00 SGD fee cannot stand because the driver never satisfied POL-NS-23's contact obligation, which is conjunctive: before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05070) contains no driver-authored message before the 16:13:40 cancellation, and the trip record's derived contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 with an empty messages array, while its own 'obligation_met' value is false. The message limb fails, so POL-NS-23 voids the fee: FULL_REFUND of the fee charged with no driver compensation.

The only pre-cancellation entry in the entire chat log is MSG-05070-001 at 16:07:28, 'Your driver has arrived.' That entry's sender is SYSTEM - the app's automatic arrival notification - and POL-NS-23 requires a chat message the driver sent to the rider. A machine-generated notification is not a driver message, and the driver's own statement concedes the point by relying on the fact that 'the app also sends the arrived notification automatically'.

The driver's assertion that he 'also sent message' is contradicted on the record. The chat log is COMPLETE with no issues at weight 1.0, contiguous and matching trip_record.chat_message_count = 3; the only driver-authored message, MSG-05070-002 ('I cancel already, you never come down'), was sent at 16:13:55 - fifteen seconds AFTER the 16:13:40 cancellation. POL-NS-23 requires the message to precede trip_record.cancelled_at, so a post-cancellation message cannot cure the omission.

The two in-app calls at 16:09:30 and 16:11:50 (both unanswered, recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls) satisfy only the call limb of POL-NS-23. The clause states the obligation in the conjunctive and does not excuse the message limb where the rider could not be reached by phone - on the rider's account she was in the shower. The driver sent no message on the in-app channel at all before cancelling, so the fee is voided.

Escalation under POL-GEN-26 is not available on this record: the fact POL-NS-23 turns on - whether the driver messaged before cancelling - is carried by two COMPLETE artifacts, the trip record and the chat log, each with no issues and weight 1.0, so nothing on that point is missing or impaired. The one absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05070-01, is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) and carries nothing about in-app contact. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band, and neither party carries a fraud flag, so this case is decidable on the record.

Party history is context only under POL-GEN-01: ratings, account ages, cancellation rates and prior flags on either profile can neither establish a fact about TRP-05070 nor decide it. The only profile fields the policy permits to do anything are the two fraud-flag fields (POL-GEN-22, which raises the confidence an AI ruling needs and never decides a trip) and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d (POL-NS-25, a referral that never changes the ruling) - and no fraud flag is set on either party. The outcome therefore turns on the contact record alone.

The ruling follows directly from the voided fee. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00 SGD and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the rider has not been made whole. Under POL-GEN-03 the rider, as the filing party, is entitled to the whole contested amount - FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD with driver_compensation_sgd null - and POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome is confined to the case 'where the fee stands', which it does not.

The driver was physically at the pickup when he marked arrival, and the GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.16 m away — well inside the STANDARD zone's 50 m arrival radius — the driver reports 25 fixes with no gap over 120 s, and the trace shows his vehicle stationary at the pickup from 16:07:20 onward. POL-NS-21's arrival test is therefore satisfied: the trip record's arrival event (16:07:25) is GPS-corroborated.

The free wait was fully served. The driver arrived at 16:07:25, the 300 s free wait ran to 16:12:25, and he did not cancel until 16:13:40 — 375 s after arrival and 75 s after the wait expired. On the on-demand branch of POL-NS-21 (no scheduled time, so the wait runs from arrival), the driver cancelled only after the policy-mandated wait had elapsed.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on the record: the driver placed two in-app calls to the rider, at 16:09:30 (rang 25 s, unanswered) and 16:11:50 (rang 20 s, unanswered), both inside the free-wait window and both before the 16:13:40 cancellation. These are in-app calls recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls, exactly the form POL-NS-23 requires.

The substantive ground for a no-show charge is made out independently of the contact formality: the rider never boarded, and her own only chat reply — 'What? I was coming down now' — was sent at 16:14:30, after both the expiry of the free wait and the cancellation. Where the no-show fee stands, POL-NS-22 fixes the outcome as DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd each equal to the 5.00 SGD charged, and POL-GEN-03 confirms that is a driver-side win, not a restoration of a charge.

The amount charged is exactly the amount the policy schedules: the payments ledger shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, matching POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee, and the fee-matches-policy derivation is true. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check has nothing to act on, so no referral on the amount arises and the fee is not exposed to a discrepancy argument.

I do not press — and must honestly concede — the message limb of POL-NS-23. The complete chat log (3 entries, contiguous, weight 1.0, matching trip_record.chat_message_count) carries no driver in-app message before the 16:13:40 cancellation: the driver's only message, 'I cancel already, you never come down', is timestamped 16:13:55 (15 s after cancellation), and the 16:07:28 'Your driver has arrived.' entry is a SYSTEM notification, not a message sent by the driver. The driver's counterparty statement that he 'sent message' is therefore corroborated only as to the two calls, not as to any pre-cancellation message, and on the strict terms of POL-NS-23 that limb is absent from this record.
